title: ERP · Unified clinical workspace
brief: Offline Spanish-language staff ERP demo for fictional Clínica Dental Andina. Full editable-master create/detail/edit/confirmed-delete for physicians, specialties, rooms, modality-filtered study types, disease/allergy references, configuration Triage, tariffs, patients, inventory and local roles. Triage requires unique trimmed classification and plain description, not patient assessment. Reference deletion protects linked clinical/financial records; stable IDs, integer cents and issued snapshots remain. Existing history/habits, appointment, consultation, studies, cash/non-payable QR and DEMO receipts preserved. S12 complete: provider layer removed entirely; direct laboratory/imaging study CRUD has implicit menu modality, name and price, and requests need only a valid catalog type. In-memory only; reload resets. S14–S16/S18 with S22–S26 exceptions: contextual Agregar Laboratorio/Agregar Imagen and CRUD labels; Imagenología sidebar; Resumen menu/page/breadcrumb with unchanged financial semantics. Agregar + is visible at the upper right of addable module/section headers. Modal actions and Configuration tabs/save show readable text, without icon-square clipping. Other actions retain semantic SVG-only content, accessible names, 44px targets and hover/keyboard-focus top-layer tooltips. Patient detail/chart use distinct eye/file geometries; all 17 sidebar SVG geometries are distinct. S17: Pagos posts outgoing expenses through a validated integer-cent ledger, seeded once with Bs 250; list/search/category filter/detail, reference-day KPI/net/chart updates, safe-aggregate guards and negative net allowed. No edit/delete of posted financial transactions. S19–S20: branded responsive no-credential simulated entry; initially hidden/inert workspace; desktop/mobile logout reloads the same file and discards all records, preferences and pending QR. No credentials read, tokens or durable session. S25 seeds one stable-ID fictional example per previously empty laboratory/imaging/reference/Triage catalog, plus representative Celia history through the existing context allocator. New patients remain undocumented; no seed orders/consultations/payments and financial baseline 700/250/450/1400 unchanged. S27 implements one explicit boolean Acceder map across all 17 stable menu IDs per role, with shared CRUD modal/detail and an always-available desktop/mobile Simular rol selector. Demo seeds: Administrator all17, Receptionist Resumen/Pacientes/Agenda/Cobros/Pagos, Doctor Resumen/Pacientes/Agenda/Atención clínica; custom roles default allfalse. Strict true grants intersect personal visibility in central navigation; denied crosslinks fail safely, revoked views fall back to first permitted menu or clear no-modules recovery. Last Administrator Configuration revocation rejects without mutation; protected Administrator and active-profile deletion guards remain. No competing legacy permission model, real authentication or server authorization. S28 adds separate strict boolean finance/agenda/clinical Resumen content capabilities tied to stable role IDs, never role names: Administrator all three, Doctor agenda/clinical, Receptionist agenda, custom roles none. Menu Acceder remains required. Only granted visible blocks render; financial KPIs/chart/prose/table/shortcuts are absent from unauthorized rendered Resumen, not CSS-hidden. Consulta indicators count reference-day appointment lifecycle without diagnosis or own-doctor inference. Personalizar Resumen uses a native text-control modal for permitted-block visibility/order and draft reset/cancel; preferences are closure-only per simulated role ID, never actual multi-user settings. Revoked grants override/prune preferences; all-hidden/zero-grant recovery and reload/logout reset remain explicit. Fictional payload remains in HTML; real API/resource authorization is future work. S1-S28 verified at prototype scope. HTTP smoke PASS 1920 checks/20 own HTML loads/zero external/API/storage writes or page errors; parent-observed RED exit1 after51 checks. Independent combined S27/S28 verification PASS60/2 own baseline/candidate GETs/no violations, plus native-click persistent-URL acceptance. Desktop/mobile/login screenshots refreshed. Native assessment unavailable due unrelated untracked declarations; no native approval or production clinical/payment/security readiness.

artboards.title: Unified business workspace
artboards.tradeoff: Complete editable-master CRUD and configuration-only Triage in the preserved single shell and connected clinical/receipt demo. Entity-specific provider-free Laboratorio/Imagenología CRUD and requests with reference protection. Upper-right Agregar +, readable modal actions and Configuration tabs/save; other row actions reveal icon explanations on hover/focus. Patient detail/chart icons differ; sidebar retains 17 distinct labeled semantic SVGs. Default module examples are fictional and reset on reload; new patient clinical data stays empty. Acceder per-menu matrix and explicit demo profile inspection control simulated visibility/routes, intersecting personal preferences; unknown/missing grants fail closed. No-modules recovery and last-Administrator validation are explicit. S28 configurable finance/agenda/clinical content grants are independent of names/menu access; only allowed blocks render, with per-simulated-role-ID hide/order preferences in a native modal. Revoked grants cannot be bypassed by preferences; zero-grant views have no financial fallback. Indicators are clinic-wide operational counts, not physician-linked data. Client-only visibility cannot protect the downloaded fictional payload. S28 full HTTP1920, independent permissions60 and actual persistent-URL checks passed; screenshots refreshed. No native approval claimed. Pagos outgoing ledger drives Resumen expenses/net/chart without changing incoming Cobros/QR semantics. No-credential simulated login and desktop/mobile logout with full reload reset. Posted expenses are not editable/deletable; fixed reference date only. No real medicine, payment, authentication/authorization, backend or persistence.
